notes:
• D&D 5e: items named in the color of their rarity. An uncommon item's name is green, a rare one's blue, a very rare one's purple, a legendary one's orange and an artifact's tan, as D&D Beyond colors them. It is so on the D&D 5e character, NPC and vehicle sheets, in their lists and among a character's favorites, and wherever the projection names an item: the Inventory tab, a weapon among the attacks, a favorite, and what the quick search finds. Common things, and things with no rarity, keep the ordinary ink. D&D Beyond's own green and orange are used as they are on a dark sheet or panel; its other colors are lightened there, and all five are darkened on a light sheet, the Journal, the Grove and the Crystal core, only as far as it takes for each to be read. An item that has not been identified is not colored, since its color would say what it is. The projection's readout also says an item's rarity in words. A new setting, on by default, switches it off.
  • D&D 5e: unprepared spells are grayed. On a character's sheet and in the projection, on the Spells tab and among the favorites, a spell that has to be prepared and is not is grayed. It can still be read, prepared and cast. Cantrips, spells that are always prepared, and spells that need no preparing (pact magic, innate spells, spells cast from an item) are not grayed. An NPC's spells are left as they were. A new setting, on by default, switches it off.
  • D&D 5e: a vitals panel that holds what is in it. On the Vambrace and its looks, the Crystal core, the omni-tool, the Armored gauntlet and the Comm unit, the six death saves and the six levels of exhaustion were wider than their cells and the last of them were cut off, and on several of those the panel was a few pixels too tall and scrolled. A track of six now closes up to fit its cell. And every panel of cells is now measured once it is drawn: a label too wide for its cell, as "Inspiration" is in a wider font than the device's own, is set a little smaller, and a panel too tall for its place is drawn a little smaller as a whole, so nothing is cut off whatever font a player has chosen.

Full details in the release notes.
